title: MCP Server (2026-07-28) Secure Architecture & Design Patterns

patterns.title: Server-Bound Credential Isolation & Per-Route Auth Dispatch
patterns.failure_mode: Forwarding MCP client Authorization tokens upstream causes confused-deputy privilege escalation; attaching a single global server credential to every route leaks tokens to public security: [] endpoints and over-privileges read tools.
invariants: Upstream credentials MUST resolve exclusively from server-side environment variables or secret stores, never from MCP client headers or tool inputSchema parameters.
Explicitly unauthenticated OpenAPI operations (security: []) MUST send zero upstream auth headers.
Multi-scheme APIs MUST dispatch credentials per (HTTP method, path template) over a single connection pool rather than instantiating per-call HTTP clients.
anti_patterns: Copying request.headers['authorization'] from an incoming Streamable HTTP MCP request onto the outbound httpx.AsyncClient.
Adding api_key or bearer_token parameters to @tool signatures so the LLM supplies credentials in plaintext tool calls.
verification_gates: Static AST + schema gate blocking sensitive parameter names (token, secret, password, api_key, authorization) in tool inputSchema.
Contract test proving /health (security: []) emits zero auth headers while /admin/* dispatches isolated scheme credentials.

field_origin.evidence: src/auth.py RouteDispatchAuth + tests/forge/test_per_op_auth.py enforcing per-operation OpenAPI security routing.

patterns.title: Immutable Chassis & Narrow Agent Overlay (Anti-Reward-Hacking)
patterns.failure_mode: Autonomous coding agents given write access to auth middleware, pyproject.toml, or contract tests bypass failing gates by deleting assertions or lowering coverage thresholds rather than fixing generated domain code.
invariants: Security-critical server chassis files (auth, lifespan DI, response middleware, contract tests, validator scripts) MUST remain read-only during tool synthesis.
Agent write permissions MUST be restricted strictly to stateless domain tool modules (src/tools/*.py), unit tests (tests/unit/*.py), and user documentation.
Host-mode synthesis MUST verify pre/post cryptographic SHA-256 digests of every locked file and abort with restoration on any mutation.
anti_patterns: Running an autonomous coding agent against a full repository root with writable test gates and trusting prompt instructions alone ('please do not edit tests').
Relying solely on POSIX chmod 0444 without SHA-256 digest verification when the agent runs as the file owner (who can call chmod +w).
verification_gates: Container synthesis mounts workspace root :ro and bind-mounts only src/tools and tests/unit :rw with --cap-drop=ALL.
LockedWorkspaceDigest SHA-256 pre/post snapshot check raising TamperDetectionError on byte drift.

field_origin.evidence: forge/orchestrator.py LockedWorkspaceDigest + golden-template/ read-only split verified in tests/forge/test_host_agent_mode.py.

patterns.title: Dual-Axis Structured Payload Bounding (Cardinality + Byte Budget)
patterns.failure_mode: Stock response-limiting middleware strips outputSchema=None on tools/list, while string-only truncation fails flat when an upstream endpoint returns 3,000 short 10-byte strings (~150 KiB) that exceed context budgets without any single string reaching 16 bytes.
invariants: Response-bounding middleware MUST preserve JSON Schema 2020-12 outputSchema declarations on tools/list.
Oversized structured payloads MUST first slice collection cardinality (list[:k], k >= 1) so array item schemas (list[Model], list[int], list[str]) remain strictly valid.
Remaining byte overages MUST shrink long UTF-8 string leaves proportionally and raise an actionable ToolError if irreducible non-string scalar structures still exceed max_bytes.
anti_patterns: Using stock middleware that erases outputSchema to fall back to unstructured text truncation.
Truncating raw serialized JSON text mid-payload, producing malformed JSON and violating structuredContent contracts.
Bounding only individual string lengths >= 16 bytes while ignoring list cardinality.
verification_gates: Contract check asserting every registered tool exposes a non-null JSON Schema 2020-12 outputSchema.
Torture test feeding 3,000 10-byte IDs (~150 KiB) and asserting bounded output <= 32,768 bytes while still validating against outputSchema.

field_origin.evidence: src/server.py ForgeResponseLimitingMiddleware + Plan 03 W4.4 dual-axis list-cardinality + UTF-8 string bounding.

patterns.title: Cycle-Safe & Polymorphic Schema Projection
patterns.failure_mode: Wild OpenAPI 3.x specs trigger SSRF on remote $refs, path traversal on '../' file $refs, infinite recursion on cyclic User.manager -> User schemas, empty {id, status} stubs on allOf/oneOf schemas, or drop nested data arrays (rows, datapoints) behind metadata timestamps.
invariants: Schema normalizers MUST reject remote URI schemes (http://, https://) and confine relative file $refs strictly inside spec_root.resolve().
Recursive $ref graphs MUST track an active ancestor pointer set (ancestor_refs) and break cycles deterministically into shallow {id: string} stubs.
allOf property maps and nullable oneOf/anyOf unions MUST be flattened prior to projection, and structural data-carrier arrays (rows, series, datapoints) MUST outrank generic audit timestamps.
anti_patterns: Resolving arbitrary $ref URLs over the network during OpenAPI ingestion (build-time SSRF).
Using a naive integer recursion depth limit without an ancestor cycle set, causing valid self-referential schemas to fail normalization.
Emitting dict[str, Any] passthrough output models that dump 100+ raw upstream fields into LLM context.
verification_gates: Unit tests verifying http:// and ../outside.yaml $refs raise normalization errors.
Unit tests verifying cyclic User -> User and allOf composed schemas resolve cleanly with data-carrier fields preserved.

field_origin.evidence: forge/ingest_openapi.py, forge/projection.py, and Plan 03 W4.1-W4.2 cycle-safe polymorphic normalization.

patterns.title: Composite Intent Tools & Active Toolset Budgets over CRUD Mirrors
patterns.failure_mode: Mapping 1 REST endpoint = 1 MCP tool forces 6-10 sequential LLM round-trips to join foreign keys for a single triage question, while mounting multiple sharded CRUD servers simultaneously floods the client context past 15 tools.
invariants: Each active client toolset profile MUST expose <= 15 tools so tool-selection accuracy and prompt token overhead stay bounded.
Multi-endpoint read/triage workflows SHOULD aggregate upstream fan-out/joins server-side over a pooled async HTTP client (e.g., asyncio.gather) and return a single task-oriented summary model.
Destructive or mutating operations MUST carry explicit ToolAnnotations (destructiveHint=True) and remain isolated from read-only triage profiles unless signed off.
anti_patterns: Auto-generating 80 raw CRUD tools from an enterprise OpenAPI spec and mounting all shards into a single agent session.
Forcing the LLM to resolve N+1 foreign-key lookups across separate MCP tool calls.
verification_gates: Manifest gate rejecting any single server or active client profile exceeding 15 tools.
Governance artifact gate flagging destructiveHint=True tools for explicit AppSec signoff.

field_origin.evidence: forge/ingest_openapi.py MAX_TOOLS_PER_SERVER=15, forge/orchestrator.py governance signoff, and Plan 03 W5.1 x-mcp-workflows.

patterns.title: Stateless Sessionless Execution & Lifespan Async DI Safety
patterns.failure_mode: Storing pagination cursors or tenant state in module globals causes cross-caller data bleed under SEP-2567 sessionless HTTP, while synchronous dependency-injection getters returning an active httpx.AsyncClient cause DI frameworks to re-enter __aenter__ and crash.
invariants: Tool modules MUST contain zero mutable module-level state; all pagination cursors, filters, and idempotency keys MUST pass explicitly via tool arguments and structured outputs.
Servers MUST support stateless SEP-2575 server/discover and SEP-2567 sessionless Streamable HTTP without sticky Mcp-Session-Id affinity.
Lifespan-pooled async HTTP clients MUST be injected via an async def dependency provider so async context managers are never re-entered per request.
anti_patterns: Caching LAST_CURSOR or CURRENT_USER in a Python module global inside src/tools/.
Instantiating a fresh httpx.AsyncClient() inside every @tool call (exhausting ephemeral sockets and TLS handshakes) or returning the lifespan client from a sync def getter.
verification_gates: AST audit forbidding mutable global assignments in src/tools/*.py.
Lifespan integration test executing concurrent tool calls over a single shared httpx.AsyncClient.

field_origin.evidence: src/deps.py async def get_http_client() + src/server.py lifespan pool.

patterns.title: Primitive RFC 9110 x-mcp-header Mirroring (Non-Union Contract)
patterns.failure_mode: Unvalidated x-mcp-header names enable HTTP header injection, mirroring secret fields leaks credentials in transport metadata, and typing optional header parameters as str | None emits JSON Schema anyOf—causing mcp==2.3.0 to silently drop the tool from tools/list.
invariants: x-mcp-header names MUST match RFC 9110 §5.1 token syntax (1*tchar: ^[!#$%&'*+\-.^_`|~0-9A-Za-z]+$).
x-mcp-header MUST NEVER be attached to credential/PII fields (token, key, secret, password, authorization, cookie, ssn) or non-primitive types (object, array, number).
Optional x-mcp-header parameters MUST use non-union primitive defaults (e.g., str = '') rather than nullable anyOf unions (str | None) so MCP SDK schema filters retain the tool.
anti_patterns: Declaring idempotency_key: Annotated[str | None, Field(default=None, json_schema_extra={'x-mcp-header': 'Idempotency-Key'})] in FastMCP / mcp==2.3.0.
Mirroring Authorization or X-Api-Key via x-mcp-header.
verification_gates: Contract test asserting tools/list count equals manifest count and no x-mcp-header property contains anyOf/oneOf.
Validator test rejecting non-tchar header names, sensitive parameter names, and complex types.

field_origin.evidence: forge/ingest_openapi.py TCHAR_RE + src/tools/create_incident.py Idempotency-Key non-union pattern.

patterns.title: Layered OS Sandboxing, SEP-2577 Hygiene & STDIO Frame Integrity
patterns.failure_mode: A single stray print() on stdout corrupts JSON-RPC framing over stdio, deprecated SEP-2577 calls fail 2026-07-28 clients, and teams mistake static AST bans on 'import os' for an actual security boundary when executing untrusted code.
invariants: MCP stdio servers MUST reserve stdout strictly for JSON-RPC frames and emit structured JSON logs exclusively to stderr.
2026-07-28 tools MUST NOT invoke deprecated SEP-2577 methods (.sample(), .list_roots(), .set_logging_level()) or embed imperative prompt-injection phrases in docstrings.

Static AST audits MUST be paired with kernel-enforced process isolation (Docker --network=none --cap-drop=ALL, macOS sandbox-exec, or Linux bubblewrap) whenever running untrusted synthesis or third-party code.
anti_patterns: Calling print() for debug logging inside a tool module or library initialization path.
Treating Python AST inspection alone as sufficient containment against adversarial code execution.
verification_gates: Ruff T20 print ban + AST SEP-2577 & docstring prompt-injection audit.
Live subprocess PythonStdioTransport server/discover probe verifying clean JSON-RPC framing over stdout/stderr.
OS/container sandbox policy enforcement (--cap-drop=ALL / sandbox-exec / bwrap) during synthesis.
